---
# GECKO Modeling Strategy Template
# Copy this file to create a new strategy.
# File naming: kebab-case matching the strategy name (e.g., multi-body-constraint.md)
#
# Strategies can be:
#   - Human-authored: written by a GECKO contributor
#   - AI-proposed: generated by the AI pipeline when a new concept doesn't fit existing strategies
#     (AI-proposed strategies should set `status: proposed` until human review)

name: "strategy-name-here"
status: stable                          # stable | proposed | deprecated
aliases: ["keyword1", "keyword2"]       # terms a user might type that map to this strategy
domains: ["physics", "biology"]         # broad subject areas
dimensionality: [2D, 3D]               # what spatial dimensions this typically uses
typical_rendering: [three.js, p5.js]    # recommended rendering libraries
language: en                            # en | es | bilingual

agent_pattern:
  description: "One sentence describing what agents represent in this strategy"
  typical_attributes: [attr1, attr2]
  typical_behaviors: [behavior1, behavior2]

environment_pattern:
  description: "One sentence describing the environment's role"
  typical_attributes: [attr1, attr2]

interaction_patterns:
  - trigger: user_action
    effect: simulation_response

visualization_hints:
  - "Hint about how to visually represent this kind of simulation"
---

# Strategy Name

## When to use this strategy

Describe the class of concepts this strategy covers. What does the user want to explore?

## Modeling reasoning

Explain *why* this decomposition works — what insight does it give the learner?

## Key mathematics / logic

Outline the core equations or rules the simulation should implement.

## Pitfalls

Common mistakes the AI should avoid when using this strategy.

## Composability

How this strategy combines with others for more complex simulators.

## Related strategies

- `other-strategy-name` — when to use that one instead
